data.long_meaning: Gowri is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘gau’ which means cow. The name signifies the goddess of agriculture, prosperity, and fertility. She is the divine mother of Lord Ganesha and is believed to have bestowed him with the elephant head. The name is also associated with Lord Shiva and Parvati. Gowri is revered for her nurturing and protective qualities and is often invoked for blessings of abundance and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Gowri is an epithet of the goddess Parvati, wife of Shiva. This name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'gaur', which means 'fair' or 'radiant'. The name is often associated with the goddess in her role as a manifestation of Shiva's consort and the mother of Kartikeya and Ganesha.

The name Gowri is also given to a star in the Ursa Major constellation, which is identified with the Hindu goddess Gauri (Parvati). In Hindu astronomy, this star is considered auspicious and is believed to bring good fortune. During the night of the star's appearance, it is customary for married women to decorate idols of the goddess with vermilion powder (kumkum) and red flowers (rakta chandana).
